programRef: ~/.claude/projects/-home-ax/memory/well-dipper-cockpit-program.md — HELM cockpit program, lane F. This workstream is increments 5–6 of the 6-increment ladder: 5 = data migration (snapshot provider, four panels live, DOM overlays retire — flagged in the ladder as 'the largest', data plumbing not visuals); 6 = zoom-to-panel. Lane E (geometry) runs concurrently and owns increments 1–4's artefacts.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The screens are the right way up AND the right way round, proved against the mesh — not against the sidecar. On every Screen_* quad in every cockpit GLB on disk, the corner carrying v=0 is the one highest off the deck, and u grows toward the pilot's right, checked PER VERTEX so a v-flip or a u-mirror turns it red. It binds to the MESH because cockpit-metrics.json's uvNote declares '(0,0) at the pilot's LOWER-LEFT corner' and the exported mesh says the opposite — otherwise someone will 'fix' the adapter from the sidecar and invert every screen. Lane E's tests/cockpit-geometry.test.js cannot catch either failure: it .sort()s the four UV pairs before comparing, discarding which vertex carried which UV. Lane F does not touch lane E's file. (The consumer half — that lane F's own uv→pixel map agrees with this — is AC-PANEL-POINTER.)

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run <lane-F-owned test file> in /home/ax/projects/well-dipper-cockpit (package.json declares test: vitest run). The test GLOBS public/assets/cockpit/*.glb rather than naming one asset, so a lane-E rename cannot silently disarm it, and asserts up front that at least one GLB carries /^Screen_/ nodes so the zero-screen state fails loudly instead of passing vacuously. For each such GLB it uses tests/helpers/glb-parse.mjs (parseGLB, which returns { json, bin } and NOT { gltf, bin }; plus readAccessor, requireNode, listNodes, nodeWorldMatrix, transformPoint), pairs each TEXCOORD_0 entry with the POSITION vertex at the SAME index, and transforms that vertex to world space. Negative case: mutate an in-memory copy of the uv array to v'=1-v and assert the check throws. The file must NOT copy lane E's describe.skipIf(missing.length > 0) pattern.
verifyVia.observable: Green run. For every Screen_* quad found: the two vertices with v=0 have strictly greater world Y than the two with v=1, and the u=1 vertices have strictly greater world X than the u=0 vertices at matching v. Both are asserted as ORDERINGS, not against baked coordinates (today's measured values, for orientation only, never as thresholds: Screen_UL v=0 at y=0.5777 vs v=1 at y=0.2889; Screen_LL v=0 at y=-0.3124 vs v=1 at y=-0.5999; Screen_UL u=1 at x=-0.7595 vs u=0 at x=-1.1212). cockpit-metrics.json states the axes as +X right, +Y up, forward -Z, eye at origin, so greater X is the pilot's right. The negative case fails as expected, proving the assertion has teeth. Grepping the lane-F file returns zero occurrences of describe.skipIf / it.skipIf / test.skip.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Pointing at the glass puts the nav cursor exactly where you're pointing — the top of the panel is the top of the picture, not the bottom — and sliding the pointer off the edge of the panel mid-drag lets go of the drag instead of leaving the map welded to the cursor. This is the consumer half of the UV convention AC-UV-ORIENTATION proves on the mesh: an adapter that uses (1 - uv.v) is the actual upside-down-screens defect Max would see, and an asset-only check cannot catch it.

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run on a NEW lane-F-owned test file (tests/cockpit-geometry.test.js is lane E's and is not touched). The test drives the lane-F pointer adapter against a stub target shaped like NavComputer: a _canvas stub {width: W, height: H} whose getBoundingClientRect() THROWS, plus spies standing in for _handleMouseDown/_handleMouseMove/_handleMouseUp. Fabricated raycast hits at uv (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (0.25,0.75); then the sequence hit→down, hit→move, ray-misses-the-quad. The whole battery runs twice at two DIFFERENT W × H so nothing can pass by hard-coding a size. Negative case: feed the mapping function the (1 - v) form and assert it throws. Separately the test asks the lane-F texture factory for a texture over a stub image {width, height}.
verifyVia.observable: uv (0,0) → (0, 0); uv (1,0) → (W, 0); uv (0,1) → (0, H); uv (0.25,0.75) → (0.25W, 0.75H). That is x = u*W and y = v*H, NOT (1 - v)*H — v=0 is the TOP edge on the Screen_* faces (glTF y-down), so top-of-panel is top-of-picture; the same relation holds at both buffer sizes, and the (1 - v) negative case fails. The stub's throwing getBoundingClientRect is NEVER called: the adapter delivers panel coords by overriding _getCanvasPos, not by synthesising clientX/clientY — NavComputer._getCanvasPos scales by (this._canvas.width / rect.width), and a canvas with no layout box gives rect.width 0, so that factor is non-finite (Infinity, or NaN when the numerator is also 0) and every coordinate is garbage. The ray-misses-the-quad step invokes the release exactly ONCE — the same NavComputer._handleMouseUp the constructor binds to BOTH 'mouseup' and 'mouseleave', and the only place this._dragging returns to false (it is assigned in exactly 3 places: init false, true in _handleMouseDown, false in _handleMouseUp). The texture comes back with flipY === false, the matching half of the same convention (three.js imports fine under the default node vitest env — 5 existing tests do it).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Which corner shows which screen is a knob, not a hard-wire: NAV, DRIVE, TARGET and SURVEY are assigned to the four Screen_* nodes in one config table, and swapping two entries swaps which panel draws where. Lane F writes down nothing about how big a screen is, what shape it is, or where it sits — that is measured off the model when it loads, and not read out of the sidecar either. If the screens aren't in the model, this goes red and says why — it never skips green. (Orientation is AC-UV-ORIENTATION's job; this AC is about binding and derivation.)

verifyVia.input: npx vitest run on a NEW lane-F-owned test file (e.g. tests/cockpit-panels.test.js). NOT tests/cockpit-geometry.test.js — that is lane E's, and its artefact block is wrapped in describe.skipIf(missing.length > 0), a pattern lane F must not copy (lane E defends it with a separate gate test; a lane-F file that copies the skipIf without the gate is green on a deleted asset). Parse the screen-bearing GLB NAMED BY LANE F'S OWN CONFIG (today public/assets/cockpit/cockpit.glb — 41 nodes, carries Screen_UL/UR/LL/LR with POSITION,NORMAL,TEXCOORD_0; lane E's newer public/assets/cockpit/cockpit-tub.glb has 14 nodes and NO Screen_* at all) using tests/helpers/glb-parse.mjs (parseGLB, requireNode, readAccessor, buildParentMap, nodeWorldMatrix, transformPoint). Run the lane-F role→node config, plus a copy with two roles permuted, through the lane-F resolver. Also readFileSync lane F's own source files and regex them for panel-dimension literals and for skip helpers.
verifyVia.observable: (1) The config maps {NAV, DRIVE, TARGET, SURVEY} bijectively onto exactly {Screen_UL, Screen_UR, Screen_LL, Screen_LR} and every named node resolves through requireNode. (2) Resolving the permuted config returns the same four node names with exactly those two roles exchanged and every other field identical. (4) With the configured GLB absent, or present but missing any Screen_* node, the lane-F suite FAILS with a readable message naming the missing node — grepping the lane-F file itself returns zero occurrences of describe.skipIf / it.skipIf / test.skip.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Inside the glass there's one ink, so the warnings can't be told apart by colour — the cue that goes on the panel carries only words and a blink, never a colour. SAFE TO DROP, SLOW DOWN and TOO CLOSE — SUBLIGHT ONLY all survive the trip with their wording intact.

The em-dash form is asserted because that is literally what SupercruiseHud.js draws; if lane F's panel font lacks the em dash, change the string in BOTH places rather than letting test and panel drift.

verifyVia.input: From /home/ax/projects/well-dipper-cockpit: (1) `npx vitest run --reporter=dot`. (2) `git diff --stat 10d5878..HEAD -- src/flight/HeadMount.js src/flight/__tests__/HeadMount.test.js src/flight/SupercruiseModel.js src/ui/SpeedFormat.js` and `git log --oneline 10d5878..HEAD -- tests/cockpit-geometry.test.js` (10d5878 is the lane-E baseline sha this was scoped against; a bare `git diff --stat` compares the WORKING TREE to HEAD and passes vacuously the moment lane F commits, so the range is load-bearing). (3) a NEW lane-F-owned test file that builds a table of state objects in the exact field shape main.js hands `scHud.update({visible, speed, commandedSpeed, driveOn, sublightCap, massLockHint, throttle, deflection, targetPos, targetDistance, aimOnTarget, captureSphere, dropMaxSpeed, dropState, flightMode, showReticle})` and runs each row through the lane-F panel readout builder, comparing against the four headless-safe exports plus the branch table transcribed below. NOTE: `SupercruiseHud.update` itself CANNOT be called from this test — its constructor does `document.createElement('canvas')` + `getContext('2d')`, its body reads `innerWidth`/`innerHeight`, and the drop labels sit behind `this._project(state.targetPos)`. Only `etaVisible`, `formatSpeed`, `speedToBarFrac`, `sublightBarFrac` are importable headlessly; everything else is a TRANSCRIBED truth table, and the transcription below is the assertion.
verifyVia.observable: (1) The `Test Files` line reads `15 failed | 120-or-more passed`, every failing path starts `vendor/motion-test-kit/` and every message is `No test suite found in file`; the `Tests` line reads `1670-or-more passed | 4 skipped` and carries NO `failed` segment at all — that is the literal shape of a clean run here, do not look for a `0 failed` token, vitest does not print one. `src/flight/__tests__/HeadMount.test.js` > 'ship trajectory is bit-identical with and without freelook input' and every test in `tests/cockpit-geometry.test.js` are among the passes. (2) `git diff --stat` reports zero changed lines across all four flight/format paths, and `git log` lists no lane-F commit touching `tests/cockpit-geometry.test.js` — lane F did not make the suite green by loosening lane E's test or by moving the flight physics. (3) For every table row, with `speed = state.speed || 0`, `hasTarget = !!state.targetPos`: the panel's speed readout equals `(speed < 0 ? 'REV ' : '') + formatSpeed(speed).value + ' ' + formatSpeed(speed).unit` character-for-character (the `REV ` prefix is part of the port, `formatSpeed` already abs-es); a SUBLIGHT tag appears iff `state.driveOn === false`; the bar fill equals `sublightBarFrac(speed, state.sublightCap || 1)` on a bipolar centre-zero scale when `driveOn === false` and `speedToBarFrac(Math.abs(speed))` otherwise (`speedToBarFrac` is NOT abs-safe — passing raw `speed` is the defect this clause catches); the commanded pin sits at `speedToBarFrac(state.commandedSpeed || 0)` un-abs'd; a drop tick appears iff `hasTarget && state.dropMaxSpeed != null`, at `speedToBarFrac(state.dropMaxSpeed)`; the speed BAND state is 'too-fast' iff `state.dropState === 'too-fast'`, else 'in-window' iff `state.dropState === 'in-window' || (hasTarget && state.dropMaxSpeed != null && speed <= state.dropMaxSpeed)`, else 'normal' (a three-state enum, not a colour — Phosphor has one ink, so lane F asserts the STATE and is free to encode it however); an ETA line is emitted iff `hasTarget && state.aimOnTarget`, reading `M:SS` from `state.targetDistance / speed` when `etaVisible({speed, targetDistance, aimOnTarget})` is true and the literal `--:--` when it is false; it prints 'SAFE TO DROP' iff `hasTarget && state.dropState === 'in-window'` and 'SLOW DOWN' iff `hasTarget && state.dropState === 'too-fast'` — these two are NOT the band formula above, the overlay deliberately uses the raw `dropState` enum for the labels and the wider `inWindow` OR only for the bar colour; a `MODE: <UPPERCASE>` line iff `state.flightMode` is truthy; and the mass-lock line reads exactly `TOO CLOSE — SUBLIGHT ONLY` (em dash) iff `state.massLockHint`. ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, asserted as a divergence: the overlay additionally gated ETA and both drop labels on `this._project(state.targetPos)` returning non-null (target on screen, in front of camera). A panel is not world-anchored, so the port drops that gate and `hasTarget` alone is the condition — the test asserts the panel DOES emit the label for an off-screen target where the overlay would have suppressed it.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The screens read the game through ONE read-only feed, taken once a frame. No panel reaches into main.js on its own — the only game data a panel sees is what the feed hands it. Change something real — commit a target, move the throttle, cut the drive, focus a different planet — and the next snapshot shows it. Poke the snapshot anywhere, at any depth, and the ship doesn't move.

verifyVia.input: chrome-devtools on the running game at the lane-F dev server Max starts, path /well-dipper/index.html (vite.config.js sets base:'/well-dipper/' so the root path 404s; it pins NO server.port and package.json's dev script is a bare `vite`, so the port is whatever Max's `npm run dev` reports — do not assume one). evaluate_script against a lane-F debug hook exposed on window in the same style as the existing window._getReticleState / window._sc / window._autopilot / window._warpTarget / window._navSubsystem hooks in src/main.js. NOTE: _navComputer, system, focusIndex, _selectedTarget and playerGalacticPos are module-level `let`s in src/main.js and are NOT on window, so the lane-F hook is the only console reach to them; this hook does not exist yet and is the single largest unbuilt dependency of this cluster. Steps: (1) take snapshot A; (2) walk A recursively and attempt an assignment on every object and array at every depth, including any nested body / system / target objects; (3) re-read the live sources through the EXISTING hooks — window._sc.model (SupercruiseModel .speed, .throttle, .driveOn, .speedCap(), .turnRateCap()), window._getReticleState().selected, window._warpTarget — and take a FRESH snapshot; (4) drive real changes (commit a target with the reticle, step the throttle, toggle the drive with setDrive, focus a different planet) and take snapshot B; (5) grep lane F's own panel-content source files for direct reads of `window._sc`, `window._getReticleState`, `window._warpTarget`, `window._navSubsystem`.
verifyVia.observable: After the write attempts: scModel.speed/.throttle/.driveOn, window._getReticleState().selected.name and window._warpTarget are identical to their pre-write values, AND the fresh snapshot taken in step 3 still reports the pre-write values — so no attempted write landed on a leaked live reference (the real hazard; whether the object is Object.freeze'd is an implementation choice, not the property being asserted, and deep-freezing every frame at 60Hz may profile badly). Snapshot B differs from A in exactly the fields whose game state was changed and in no others. The step-5 grep returns zero hits in every panel-content file — the only file allowed to name a window hook or a main.js binding is the snapshot provider itself. Zero console errors across the run.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Each of the four screens shows its charter content and it is live, not a mock-up. DRIVE shows speed in the same km/s → Mm/s → c tiers the current HUD uses, the throttle, drive on/off, the MODE: line, and the ceilings the ship is actually flying under. TARGET keeps the selected body's name up with its raw distance, its ETA, and SAFE TO DROP / SLOW DOWN. SURVEY shows the body dossier that today only exists in the debug HUD — composition, atmosphere, tidal state — plus the equilibrium temperature that has never had a readout. NAV is showing the nav computer from the first frame after boot, with nobody having pressed anything. No screen anywhere shows fuel, hull, heat, cargo or shields, because the game has none.

verifyVia.input: chrome-devtools on the running game at the lane-F dev server, path /well-dipper/index.html (base '/well-dipper/'; no port is pinned in vite.config.js — use the port Max's server reports). Boot into HELM and, BEFORE touching anything, read the NAV panel back through the lane-F debug hook. Then commit a target and fly one leg: drive on, throttle up through the tiers, close on the target through the drop window, drive off and throttle through zero into reverse; then focus a planet, then a moon, then clear focus. At three sampled moments read each panel's content model back through the lane-F hook AND take_screenshot of the glass. Cross-check: DRIVE against formatSpeed(scModel.speed) from src/ui/SpeedFormat.js, against SupercruiseModel .throttle / .driveOn / .speedCap() / .turnRateCap(), and against the SAME flightMode value main.js already feeds scHud (`flightMode: _scManual ? _flightMode : null`, values from FlightMode in src/flight/flightModes.js) — SupercruiseHud renders `MODE: ${state.flightMode.toUpperCase()}` from that raw string and does NOT route through flightModeInfo. TARGET against window._getReticleState().selected.name; the distance against scModel.position.distanceTo(_resolveSelectedBody().mesh.position), the same expression main.js feeds scHud as targetDistance; the ETA against SupercruiseHud's ACTUAL gate (the counter LINE draws whenever state.aimOnTarget is true, showing '--:--' unless etaVisible({speed, targetDistance, aimOnTarget}) is true, in which case it is M:SS = targetDistance / speed); the drop label against _scDropState().state ('in-window' → SAFE TO DROP, 'too-fast' → SLOW DOWN, 'none' → neither). SURVEY (now the INFO panel) against the focused body's physics (composition, atmosphere, tidalState — the same objects DebugPanel reads as entry.planet.physics) plus that planet's data.T_eq from PlanetGenerator. AMENDED 2026-07-28, two changes: (1) surfaceHistory is DROPPED — Max agreed; it is byte-identical across every planet in a system (three distinct objects, one set of values, verified on seeds 'test-alpha' and 'Aletheia'), so the row carried no information, and the space goes to T_eq which does vary. Do not look for it; the snapshot no longer carries it. (2) The atmosphere cross-check was VACUOUS as originally written: src/main.js built planetPhysics from entry.planetData.atmosphereRetained, a key PlanetGenerator has never emitted (the only occurrence of that name in PlanetGenerator.js is a parameter into habitabilityScore), so physics.atmosphere was null on every planet in the galaxy and 'panel matches source' compared null to null and passed while showing the pilot nothing. Fixed to read entry.planetData.atmosphere?.physics. Cross-check against THAT, and treat a blank ATMO row on a world with a retained atmosphere as a failure. The no-invented-gauges check is over RENDERED LABELS collected from the four content models, NOT a source grep — 'hull' is pervasive in this repo as cockpit geometry (Hull_Nose, HULL_REF_LENGTH, HULL_NAMES), so /fuel|hull|heat|cargo|shield/i over source is unusable.
verifyVia.observable: At all three samples each panel's rendered text equals the value computed from the live source — same tier, same unit string, same rounding as formatSpeed returns (km/s: 1-dp under 100 else integer with thousands separators; Mm/s: 2-dp; c: 2-dp under 100 else integer). The REV prefix appears exactly when speed < 0 (formatSpeed itself returns a magnitude — it takes Math.abs — so the sign is the panel's job, exactly as it is SupercruiseHud's today). The SUBLIGHT tag appears exactly when driveOn === false. TARGET's name persists across frames where the aim point leaves the body; its drop label flips exactly when _scDropState().state flips; the ETA line is present exactly when aimOnTarget is true, reading '--:--' when etaVisible is false and M:SS when it is true. SURVEY's composition / atmosphere / tidalState fields match getPhysicsSummary() for the focused body; T_eq matches data.T_eq for a focused PLANET, and reads BLANK — not stale, not 0 — for a focused moon, a focused star, and when focusIndex is -1 (PlanetGenerator writes T_eq onto planet data only; moons and stars carry none). NAV's backing buffer has non-background pixels in the FIRST frame after boot with no input, and the level it reports equals NavComputer's LEVELS[_levelIndex] (module-level const ['galaxy','sector','region','prism','system'], not exported; _levelIndex starts at 3 = prism) and follows when _levelIndex is driven through the lane-F hook. No panel's label set contains FUEL, HULL, HEAT, CARGO or SHIELD. Zero console errors.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The nav computer really lives on its CRT — it draws at that panel's own resolution and keeps drawing there, instead of going black the instant its canvas stops being a page element. And the old full-screen nav overlay never opens.

verifyVia.input: Max starts the dev server (no port is pinned in vite.config.js — use the one he reports). Load /well-dipper/ in HELM and wait for the cockpit and its Screen_* panels to be in the scene. Sit in the default helm view with NO panel zoomed and give the panel no input. Take a chrome-devtools screenshot, then evaluate_script TWICE ~5s apart: (1) const c = window._navComputer._canvas; [c.width, c.height]; (2) ink coverage — sample window._navComputer._ctx.getImageData(0,0,c.width,c.height) and report the fraction of pixels whose RGB differs from the pixel at (0,0); (3) const o = document.getElementById('nav-computer-overlay'); o ? getComputedStyle(o).display : 'absent'. Position language is deliberately 'the panel the loader binds NAV to' — nothing in Max's charter maps NAV to a specific quadrant, and lane E is re-fitting screens.
verifyVia.observable: Both samples report the SAME [width, height], both non-zero, and NOT the 800x800 authored on <canvas id="nav-computer-canvas"> in index.html — i.e. a panel-derived buffer size was injected and it survived. Ink coverage is > 0 on BOTH reads. That second read is the whole point: NavComputer.render()'s first statement is this._resizeCanvas(), and NavComputer._resizeCanvas assigns canvas.width/height from this._canvas.getBoundingClientRect(), which on a canvas with no layout box reports 0x0 — so an implementation that injects the size once at setup reads non-zero on sample 1 and 0x0 with zero ink on sample 2. The overlay probe returns 'absent' or 'none' (DIEGETIC-ONLY: the DOM nav overlay never opens). Detachment is NOT asserted — an offscreen canvas in a hidden container, or an OffscreenCanvas transfer, satisfies the ruling equally. The screenshot shows nav-computer drawing on one of the cockpit's screens.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Lane F binds to the surface, never to the pose. Every panel's size, aspect, place and existence comes out of whatever cockpit GLB is loaded, and the proof is that CHANGING the screen geometry changes the panels with no lane-F edit. Load the model that has screens and four panels appear filling exactly those quads. Load the same model with its Screen_* vertices scaled to a different size and aspect and the panels follow, still filling them exactly. Load lane E's screenless tub and the cockpit still comes up clean with zero panels and no errors.

verifyVia.observable: Three distinct outcomes from one unedited host. (a) cockpit.glb: four lit panels, each coincident with its Screen_* quad, no gap, overhang or stretch; reported aspect equal to what the CURRENT asset measures — AMENDED 2026-07-29, it was written as 1.5 against the 0.450 x 0.300 model and today's cockpit.glb measures 0.240 x 0.200, aspect 1.200 (6:5). The AC's ARGUMENT is untouched and is what matters: run (b), the scaled variant, is what actually falsifies hard-coding, because a host with any fixed aspect passes run (a) by construction. (b) the scaled variant: four panels still coincident, and the reported width/height/aspect DIFFER from run (a) by the same factors the vertices were scaled by. This is the half that actually falsifies hard-coding — a host with 0.45 × 0.30 baked in passes run (a) perfectly, because those are exactly the numbers cockpit-metrics.json declares, and fails run (b) with visible overhang. (c) cockpit-tub.glb: cockpit renders, zero panels created, mcp__chrome-devtools__list_console_messages returns no errors or uncaught exceptions.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The nav panel is cheap enough to leave running all the time, and it never goes dead. Sitting in the default helm view just looking at it, it repaints at a lazy ambient rate rather than pinning a frame every 16 ms. When the autopilot's drill animations run — and they are the whole screensaver — the panel does NOT re-bake its 512-square galaxy image once per frame the way today's full-screen overlay does; the number of GPU read-backs over a full galaxy→sector→region descent stays in single digits instead of tracking the frame count. And a drill started and then left alone always finishes and releases the panel: clicking works afterwards, every time, so a paused or throttled panel can never permanently deaden its own input.

verifyVia.input: Dev server (Max's port), helm view, panel unfocused. Instrument entirely from mcp__chrome-devtools__evaluate_script using the read-only window._navComputer handle NavComputer installs in its constructor — no production counters needed, because assigning to an instance shadows the prototype method: wrap window._navComputer.render to count repaints, and wrap window._navComputer._navGalaxyRenderer._renderer.readRenderTargetPixels to count cache MISSES (readRenderTargetPixels is a three.js WebGLRenderer method, reached through _navGalaxyRenderer._renderer, and it sits on the miss path only, after the this._cache.has(key) early return). Then (1) sit ambient 5 s and read the repaint count; (2) let AutopilotNavSequence run a full_journey / sector_hop leg, or drive it by writing _levelIndex and calling _startDrillAnim, so the panel descends through the 2D levels where _render2DLevel calls _renderDensityBg, and read the read-back count across it; (3) 3 s after the last drill, read window._navComputer._anim, then mcp__chrome-devtools__click the panel and read window._navComputer._levelIndex. Take the same three numbers on today's full-screen overlay as the before-baseline.
verifyVia.observable: (1) Ambient: roughly 50-75 repaints in 5 s, versus the ~300 today's requestAnimationFrame _navRenderLoop produces. (2) Across the 2D descent the read-back count stays under 10, versus a baseline on the current overlay of roughly one per rendered frame — because _startDrillAnim interpolates _viewSize continuously, _render2DLevel passes ext = viewSize/2 into NavGalaxyRenderer.render, and the cache key quantises extent to 0.01 kpc, so at galaxy and sector scales every animated frame is a fresh key, a fresh 1 MB synchronous readRenderTargetPixels, a 512-row JS pixel copy and a newly allocated 512-square canvas, against a _cacheMax of 8 that thrashes. (3) window._navComputer._anim === null and the subsequent click changes _levelIndex, proving _handleClick did not hit its 'if (this._anim) return' early exit. acceptanceCriteria.statement: With every AC above already green, Max flies the ship and says whether retiring the DOM/canvas HUD cost him anything he misses — whether everything he used to glance at is still somewhere he can glance at, whether the ship still FEELS like it flies the way it flew before the cockpit went in, whether the nav computer dithered onto NAV reads as Phosphor or as mud, and whether the whole thing coheres as the default autopilot/screensaver aesthetic he asked for.

verifyVia.input: Max, on the dev server he started, boots into HELM and flies manually for several minutes doing the things he already did: watch speed climb through the km/s → Mm/s → c tiers, ride the throttle, approach a target and watch SAFE TO DROP / SLOW DOWN, drop out and re-engage the drive with R, take and give back the stick with F, swap to ORRERY with M and back. Then he takes his hands off and lets the hands-off tour and the nav sequence run as a screensaver, and looks at the NAV panel with the existing full-colour NavComputer canvas running through the Phosphor dither. He compares against his memory of the pre-cockpit build, not against a spec.
verifyVia.observable: Max's own verdict, in his own words, on two questions no argument settles: (1) did anything he had get lost — 'I used to be able to see/feel X and now I can't'; (2) does the dithered NavComputer read as Phosphor or as mud — the H4 fork, which decides whether ~3,900 lines of NavComputer drawing code are saved or whether the screens get re-authored one at a time against a proven host, highest-traffic first (PRISM and SYSTEM). There is no snapshot field, DOM query, console probe, screenshot diff or assertion that stands in for either, and NO AGENT MAY MARK THIS PASS UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES — an agent's only permitted outcome here is `deferred-to-max`. Anything an agent could have caught belongs to the ACs above, and its appearance here means one of those was closed prematurely.

designDecisions: DIEGETIC-ONLY, and it is HELM-SCOPED. The four in-world screens REPLACE the DOM/canvas HUD overlays in HELM. Press M and ORRERY is exactly as it is today — building a second, world-space HUD for ORRERY is a different lane and a different scope interview, not this one.

The four-panel charter is settled. NAV = the nav computer, all 7 screens, autopilot drives it; zoomed = today's full-screen nav computer, operable. DRIVE = speed (3 tiers), throttle, drive on/off, MODE:, speedCap() ceiling, turnRateCap(); zoomed = expanded flight detail. TARGET = persistent selected-target name, raw targetDistance, ETA, SAFE TO DROP / SLOW DOWN; zoomed = target list / retarget. SURVEY = BodyInfo content + the physics currently only in #debug-hud (composition, atmosphere, tidalState, T_eq); zoomed = full body dossier.

The 320-square system-map / gravity-well circle FOLDS INTO NAV. NavComputer's SYSTEM level already draws a system orrery, and minimapVisible is hard-initialised false so that circle is empty at boot anyway.

Targeting brackets, the body-name label and the steering cross go on the CANOPY GLASS, not on a panel — they track world positions. A panel is not world-anchored, which is also why the port drops SupercruiseHud's this._project(targetPos) gate on the ETA and drop labels.

H4 is the hosting strategy: build the HOST first, put the EXISTING NavComputer canvas on it, run it through the Phosphor dither, and JUDGE BY EYE. The crux is NOT performance — it is that NavComputer is FULL COLOUR (per-spectral-class star colours, #00d4ff cyan you-are-here, #00ff80 selected, #ffc850 gold labels, a GPU-rendered galaxy density image) while Phosphor law is ONE INK on black. Whether that dithers into something readable is a judge-by-eye question no argument settles; it is Max's UAT gate and no agent may close it. If it reads, ~3,900 lines of drawing code are saved; if not, re-author screens one at a time against a host already proven, highest-traffic first (PRISM and SYSTEM; COMPONENT and PLANET detail are rare). The plumbing is identical either way, so nothing is wasted.

The autopilot question is ANSWERED, do not re-derive it. idleFiresTour({regime}) in src/flight/flightModes.js is literally `return regime === 'helm'`; the boot chooser maps HELM → tour armed and ORRERY → nothing armed, so ORRERY never auto-arms. During any HELM state including the hands-off tour the one camera write is scHead.applyTo(camera, scModel.position, scModel.orientation) — the camera is ON THE SHIP at the helm. HELM-gating the cockpit at setScManual() therefore covers the whole screensaver tour. Residual: startFlythrough() is still reachable with _scManual===false from four live paths (the NavComputer autopilot button, two mobile dock/speed-dial autonav buttons, the post-respawn wasAutopilot re-arm) which run with no cockpit — that is AC-NO-COCKPITLESS-AUTOPILOT's subject.

AutopilotNavSequence (src/auto/AutopilotNavSequence.js) is act two of the screensaver: autoNav.onTourComplete fires it, it scripts 5 weighted navigation styles, fakes a blinking cursor at _nav._autoCursor, drives real drill animations, then picks a star and warps. It does all that today by OPENING THE FULL-SCREEN OVERLAY. Under DIEGETIC-ONLY that overlay retires, so this entire system is homeless unless NAV hosts it — and closeNavComputer's early return is currently the ONLY path to dispatchNavAction, which is the only thing that fires the warp. Host it or the screensaver loop stops closing.

UV convention, measured off the mesh: v=0 is the TOP edge on all four Screen_* faces (glTF y-down), and u grows toward the pilot's right. So texture.flipY = false, and the raycast adapter maps y = uv.v * height, x = uv.u * width — NOT (1 - uv.v). BIND TO THE MESH, NOT THE SIDECAR: cockpit-metrics.json's uvNote declares '(0,0) at the pilot's LOWER-LEFT corner' and is wrong; someone will otherwise 'fix' the adapter from it and invert every screen. Lane E's tests/cockpit-geometry.test.js cannot see either error because it .sort()s the four UV pairs before comparing, hiding a v-flip AND a u-mirror.

Roles are bound to node names as CONFIG, and geometry is DERIVED FROM THE SEAM AT LOAD. The contract may fix node names and the UV convention; it must NOT fix panel size, aspect or position. Reading the numbers back out of cockpit-metrics.json is the same hard-coding one indirection out and is equally forbidden.

Lane E's artefacts are READ-ONLY to lane F: scripts/cockpit-gen.py, cockpit-lab.html, tests/cockpit-geometry.test.js, public/assets/cockpit/*. Lane F writes its own test files and never edits lane E's to go green.

The screen data is trapped: every feed (system, focusIndex, _selectedTarget, playerGalacticPos, scModel.speed/throttle, warpTarget, _navComputer) is a module-level `let` in a ~11k-line src/main.js with no exports and no store. A read-only snapshot provider is the FIRST work, and no panel may reach into main.js on its own. Template: the window._autopilot object; a closer snapshot-shaped example is the { selected: { kind, name } } the reticle renderer is fed.

Phosphor has NO alert vocabulary by law — monochrome inside the glass. A notification must work in ONE ink: inversion + blink. That is why the cue function returns words and a blink tier and provably carries no '#' string anywhere in its values — it is what mechanically stops the HUD's #7bff9e / #ffb84d / #ff7b6b riding along through a copy-paste port.

Most of the flight readout is a PORT WITH SEMANTICS PRESERVED, not an invention. speed tiering via SpeedFormat.formatSpeed, the log-scaled bar, the commanded-speed pin, the drop-safety tick, bipolar throttle, ETA, SAFE TO DROP / SLOW DOWN / TOO CLOSE — SUBLIGHT ONLY all already ship on the SupercruiseHud Canvas2D overlay and are physically correct. One trap that would have propagated a wrong safety cue: the LABEL branch is the raw `dropState` enum; the wider `inWindow` OR formula drives the speed BAR band only. Do not conflate them.

'Phosphor' means the general aesthetic, not the rendering tech. Ordinary bold monospace at a legible size is fine; the 5x7 A-Z alphabet is explicitly NOT required work. Ink #EDE8DE on black with a [P] colour toggle; the canopy stays on in helm mode. NOTE: the Phosphor kit does not exist in this worktree — statusReadout, lampLit, a baseline(H) helper and the H/3840 anchor return zero hits; 'Phosphor' appears only as the palette/[P] cycler in cockpit-lab.html and two dropdown options in index.html. Blink cadences (1200/600ms slow, 300/150ms fast) and the NOMINAL/ELEVATED/CRITICAL tier are hooks left open on purpose, to be authored here.

THE INFO PIPELINE IS A TABLE, AND THAT IS THE DELIVERABLE. Max: 'one panel is an info panel that gives you info about whichever system object is selected. We can expand/adjust the systems generating that info in the future; we just need a well-architected pipeline for that info to get to the screen.' So src/cockpit/InfoReadout.js is ONE table of {label, read, format} rows and adding or dropping a field is one line in one place, proved by a test that appends a row and asserts the builder picks it up with no other change. MISSING MEANS BLANK — never stale, never 0. A formatter doing (value || 0) ships a lie, and that is not hypothetical: DebugPanel.js's own composition row does exactly that. The test pins BLANK to the literal empty string, because an earlier version asserted only against the exported constant and stayed green when BLANK was changed to '0'.

DATA THAT DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE IN THE CODEBASE: fuel, hull, heat, cargo, shields. Any gauge for those invents state. No AC may require them, and no panel may label them. (The no-invented-gauges check must run over RENDERED LABELS, not a source grep — 'hull' is pervasive in this repo as cockpit geometry: Hull_Nose, HULL_REF_LENGTH, HULL_NAMES.)

Pixel and DOM assertions cannot be unit tests in this repo: package.json carries vitest with no jsdom, happy-dom or node-canvas, and NavComputer's constructor calls canvas.getContext('2d'). Every pixel check is necessarily live; every unit AC either tests a pure function or drives a NavComputer-shaped stub.

vite.config.js sets base '/well-dipper/' (the root path 404s) and pins NO server.port; the dev script is a bare `vite`. Max starts the server, never Claude, and any hard-coded port in a verification procedure is fiction.

The cursor model and hands-on flight are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE in the code as it stands: freeLookPointerRoute's free-cursor branch needs latched === true, while the W/S throttle path is gated on handRouting(_scManual && !freeLook.latched).throttle. Any 'zoom a panel by clicking it' design must therefore either take a free-look-latched precondition or introduce a new hand-state. That is a design decision, not an implementation detail — see openForMax.

ORRERY KEEPS ITS DOM HUD, UNCHANGED. Max, this session: 'leave as is'. This is deliberately a NARROWER reading of DIEGETIC-ONLY than the program memory records (which framed the only two options as world-space labels or nothing, both of which retire ORRERY's HUD): DIEGETIC-ONLY is a HELM policy. The four screens live in the cockpit; ORRERY has no cockpit, so 'diegetic' has no referent there. Reinforced by commitBurnSwapsToHelm(targetKind, scManual, isMobile) => !scManual && !isMobile && targetKind !== 'ship' — MOBILE BURNS NEVER SWAP TO HELM, so mobile players live in ORRERY permanently. (The 'ship' exclusion is currently dormant: SHIPS_ENABLED = false.) World-space ORRERY labels, if ever wanted, are a separate lane and a separate scope interview, not an edit to this contract.

ZOOMING A PANEL LATCHES FREE-LOOK; the ship coasts while you read a screen. Max, this session: 'if we're interacting with the panels it's because we've toggled off flight controls.' This makes existing behaviour explicit rather than adding a rule: freeLookPointerRoute's free-cursor branch requires latched === true, so cursor-available and W-moving-the-throttle are ALREADY mutually exclusive in the live code.

PANEL FOCUS HOTKEYS ARE Shift+1..Shift+4, MAPPED SPATIALLY TO THE CORNERS (1=UL, 2=UR, 3=LL, 4=LR). Max chose number keys; bare 1-9 are taken in HELM (autopilot ON: 1 = autoNav.jumpToStar(), 2-9 = autoNav.jumpToPlanet(n-2); autopilot OFF: 1-9 = focusPlanet(n-1)) and are player-documented in the keybinds overlay, so the modifier preserves both. Shift+Digit1..7 collides only with window._labMode.runScenario(), which requires ?lab=1. The overlay's 'SHIFT — Boost (hold with WASD)' row is STALE — there is no shift-boost path in the supercruise input chain.

A PANEL WITH AN ACTIVE ALERT ESCALATES TO THE 60Hz RENDER TIER, reusing NAV's animation-escalation mechanism. lampLit's fast blink is 300/150 ms and would alias at the ~10-15Hz ambient cadence. The alternative — slowing the blink to fit the cadence — was REJECTED: it retunes a proven, Hyte-signed-off attention grammar to accommodate an implementation detail.

DOM SURFACE FATES IN HELM (Max ruled the set, this session). #targeting-overlay: REUSED, restyled as the canopy-glass layer — it is already a fullscreen pointerEvents:none canvas drawing from world positions, and rebuilding it inside the cockpit scene buys nothing visible; one non-diegetic surface survives, but it is drawing the diegetic thing.

DOM SURFACE FATES IN HELM (cont). #nav-computer-overlay: RETIRED — zoomed NAV renders ON THE GLASS and must NOT fall back to the fullscreen overlay. If zoom reopened the overlay, the zoom would be theater and the fullscreen menu DIEGETIC-ONLY exists to kill would be back. This is the expensive answer and it is the one that matches Max's stated direction: 'have that screen move towards the camera's POV'.

DOM SURFACE FATES IN HELM (cont). #mode-swap-btn: HIDDEN in HELM, KEPT in ORRERY (M still works; in HELM you are inside a cockpit). #flight-mode-toast: RETIRED in HELM — DRIVE flashes the mode instead — KEPT in ORRERY. SystemMap / GravityWellMap in the RetroRenderer HUD pass: GONE in HELM (NAV hosts the system view), KEPT in ORRERY, still toggled by C via minimapVisible.
openForMax: Panel pixel resolution — CONFIRMED DEFERRED (Max: 'ok'). A judge-by-eye knob, like cockpit render resolution. Nothing in the contract fixes it: the buffer size is injected from the panel and the ACs assert only that it is panel-derived, non-zero and stable. Re-anchoring Phosphor's baseline(H) (hard-anchored to H/3840) means the type scale follows whatever value is picked. renderer.setPixelRatio(1) caps the ceiling regardless.
